HediffDef.label: TCCC basic training
HediffDef.description: Basic tactical casualty care training: hemostasis and casualty movement.

HediffDef.label: TCCC advanced training
HediffDef.description: Advanced tactical casualty care training: basic skills plus full-dose analgesia, hemostatic agents and MIST handovers.

HediffDef.label: applying pressure
HediffDef.description: Hemostasis is in progress on this body part. Bleeding from this part is reduced by 70% while pressure is maintained.

HediffDef.label: hemostatic agent
HediffDef.description: Reduces bleeding throughout the body by 70% for 6 hours, including new wounds. Combines with body-part hemostasis. Blood pumping -10%, consciousness -5%.

HediffDef.label: hemostasis dressing
HediffDef.description: Hemostasis skills and medic bags share this dressing. Reduces bleeding from this body part by 80% for 12 hours without tending wounds. Each dressed part adds 5% pain, up to 20% in total. Reapplication refreshes the same dressing. Combines with systemic hemostatic agents.

HediffDef.label: MIST handover prepared
HediffDef.description: Injury mechanism, injuries, signs and treatments have been recorded for evacuation. MEDEVAC arrives 25% faster if every selected patient has a current report. Loading and handover take half as long for prepared patients. Reports remain current for 6 hours.

HediffDef.label: dragging casualty
HediffDef.description: A carabiner tether allows hands-free casualty movement. Movement speed is reduced by 35%; work, aiming, cooldown and timed interactions take longer.

ThingDef.label: hemostatic agent
ThingDef.description: A field hemostatic dose carried in a large medical pouch, used to suppress systemic bleeding alongside treatment of individual wounds.
